 Warren County leaders highlight property tax deadlines, parks updates, and hazardous waste day in Fiscal Court 
 Warren County Fiscal Court update By Ananda Wallace Published : Oct. 30, 2026 at 10:34 AM CDT | Updated : 5 hours ago Share Add Us On Google Add as a preferred source on Google What This Story Is About 
 Warren County Fiscal Court highlighted three key community updates: a deadline to save money on property taxes, the revival of youth flag football alongside park playground turf upgrades, and the upcoming biannual Household Hazardous Waste Day. 
 Why It Matters 
 County homeowners can save money by taking advantage of the 2% property tax discount before the cutoff, families gain expanded recreational opportunities through the revived parks program, and residents have a free, safe method to dispose of hazardous household materials and electronics without risking local waterways. 
 What Happens Next 
 Property taxes: Payments must be made or postmarked before Sunday, Nov. 1 to receive the 2% discount. 
 Hazardous Waste Day: The collection event will run this Saturday from 8 a.m. to 1 p.m. at Lauren Avery Drive (households only; no businesses, tires, or general trash). 
 For Context 
 The property tax discount is an annual early-payment incentive offered through the sheriff’s office. Meanwhile, the county’s flag football league returned after a roughly 20-year hiatus—originally established 26 years ago—and the Division of Stormwater Management hosts its hazardous waste event biannually under grant guidelines that restrict participation strictly to residential households. 
 BOWLING GREEN, Ky. (WBKO) - Warren County Fiscal Court addressed community reminders and county services Thursday morning, highlighting an upcoming property tax discount deadline, new recreational offerings, and an upcoming hazardous waste collection event.
 Warren County Sheriff Brett Hightower reminded residents that property owners can receive a 2% discount on their property taxes if payments are made by Sunday, Nov. 1. Payments sent by mail must be postmarked before Nov. 1 to qualify for the discount.
 Parks department updates
 The Warren County Parks and Recreation Department reported progress on playground turf projects across the county and announced the launch of a new youth flag football program.
 “Chris and his Warren County PB board created a Warren County flag football program,” Chris Kummer, director of Warren County Parks and Recreation, said. “This was done all within about a four week period. They had over 256 kids playing flag football. We started flag football back 26 years ago. After a few years, it took a hiatus. So in about 20 years later, we’ve got flag football back, which is awesome. The program is going great. We had a WKU night on Tuesday with over 600 tickets sold and we had a huge turnout for the kids.”
 Household hazardous waste collection
 The Warren County Division of Stormwater Management announced its biannual Household Hazardous Waste Day to help residents dispose of materials such as latex paint, household cleaners, and batteries.
 “Same place, same time, same everything,” Nickki Koller, director of stormwater management, said. “Lauren Avery Drive, Saturday 8 to 1. We will take all your hazardous chemicals, electronic scrap. There’s some shredding options and paint. No tires at this event and no general junk and trash. Sometimes that creeps in. And no businesses. This is for households only. If you have a business, we are not legally allowed to take it per our grant requirements.”
 More information on accepted materials is available on the Warren County government website
